public_source.title: REST API endpoints for repository contents — Create or update file contents
observations: The endpoint creates a new file or replaces an existing file in a repository.
The sha body parameter is required when updating a file and identifies the blob being replaced.
The documented response family includes 409 Conflict and 422 Validation failed.
GitHub explicitly warns that create/update contents and delete-file operations used in parallel will conflict and must be serialized.

tested_scope: Official-documentation probe of duplicate/conflict safety for GitHub Contents create/update transport only. No live conflicting writes, no scheduler mutation, no other-role semantics, no checker rerun, no approval-flow test, no plan/cost test, and no 18-role coverage test were performed.

supports: Update operations expose an explicit current-blob sha compare-and-set input.

A stale or otherwise conflicting write has a documented 409 Conflict outcome, enabling fail-closed conflict detection rather than silent overwrite when callers bind updates to the current blob identity.
Serialization is explicitly required for conflicting create/update versus delete operations, so a safe design must avoid parallel mutation chains.
does_not_establish: A first-create retry after an ambiguous lost response is idempotent without an additional read/reconciliation step.
An identical replay with a stale sha is treated as success rather than conflict.
A connector-level approval-free unattended write path for every recurrence.
The exact read-after-ambiguous-result reconciliation needed to distinguish already-committed identical content from an uncommitted attempt.
Current 18-role managed-pool coverage, full-route zero incremental cost, or zero finite plan/quota dependency.
finding.reasoning: The official API contract is sufficient to support optimistic-concurrency conflict detection for updates: callers must supply the blob sha they intend to replace and conflicts have a documented 409 path. It is not sufficient to prove end-to-end duplicate-safe retry after an ambiguous result, because the endpoint documentation provides no idempotency key/replay guarantee and this slice did not verify the required follow-up read/byte-identity reconciliation. Therefore the candidate's duplicate/conflict hard gate remains false, while a narrower subclaim—CAS-style update conflict detection is available—is supported.

Preserve useful_outcome_parity=false and duplicate_conflict_safe=false.
